history.summary: CSV ERROR FLAG: there is NO distinct Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Lucknow. The famous temple is at Varanasi, about 284-324 km from Lucknow by road - the CSV town is wrong. DUPLICATE FLAG: the master CSV also contains seq 2407 'Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Varanasi' (not yet processed) - row 2385 is a duplicate entry of seq 2407; id carries the -duplicate suffix. The temple is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas on the western bank of the Ganga at Varanasi, mentioned in the Skanda Purana Kashi Khanda. Its history is a cycle of destruction and rebuilding: the original temple was demolished in the Ghori/Aibak invasion (1194), rebuilt under Iltutmish, destroyed again in the late medieval period, rebuilt by Raja Man Singh / Todar Mal under Akbar (1585), and demolished in 1669 by Aurangzeb, who built the Gyanvapi Mosque on its site. The present structure was built on an adjacent site in 1780 by Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore; in 1835 Maharaja Ranjit Singh donated a tonne of gold to plate the dome. In 2021-22 the Kashi Vishwanath Dham Corridor connecting the temple to the Ganga was inaugurated, sharply increasing pilgrim numbers.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
town: Varanasi (CSV town 'Lucknow' is WRONG - no such temple in Lucknow; the real temple is in Varanasi, ~284-324 km away)
town_description: Varanasi (Kashi/Banaras) is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, on the western bank of the Ganga, and the holiest Hindu pilgrimage city. The Kashi Vishwanath Temple stands in Vishwanath Gali in the old city, near the Ganga ghats (Lalita Ghat, Manikarnika Ghat) with which it is now connected by the Kashi Vishwanath Dham Corridor.
